SEOUL, Oct 28 : South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix reported a more than seven-fold rise in quarterly operating profit to a record high on Wednesday, beating market forecasts, as continued demand for AI infrastructure drove up memory chip prices. The Nvidia supplier also said it will pursue shareholder returns totalling about 100 trillion won ($75.4 billion) this year, comprising cash dividends of 30 trillion won and share repurchases and cancellations of 60 trillion won, including 40 trillion won announced in August. SK Hynix also reiterated that it expects demand to continue to exceed supply through 2030. To improve mid-to-long term demand visibility, SK Hynix has signed long-term agreements (LTAs) with 14 major customers, while "proactively discussing with a number of customers the possibility of extending the contract terms, which are typically five years."

MEXICO CITY, Oct 27 : Sergio "Checo" Perez will make his 300th Formula One start in front of his home fans in Mexico City, capping a career that began with a teenage move to Europe and grew alongside the sport's resurgence in his country. "Honestly, not even in my wildest dreams could I have imagined it," Perez told reporters on Tuesday about reaching the milestone at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. Perez's landmark start was moved to his home race by a reshaped calendar after the cancellations of the Saudi Arabian and Bahrain Grands Prix, with Malaysia replacing Bahrain. "Reaching so many Grands Prix will be an unforgettable moment, one that makes me very proud of my career and of the professionalism I have had".

The 35-year-old has spent more than 15 years in Formula One, having raced for Sauber, McLaren, Force India, Racing Point and Red Bull, before joining Cadillac's new project. His career highlights include his first Formula One victory in Bahrain in 2020, a Monaco Grand Prix win in 2022 and a home podium in Mexico, which he ranked as his most special moment.  Formula One returned to Mexico in 2015, after a 23-year absence, giving Perez the chance to race at home for the first time since his karting days. "Once the Mexican Grand Prix began, the sport grew enormously in our country. Before that people did not really talk about motorsport; it felt very distant," Perez added saying the race return help turn the country into one of the sport's most passionate stops. "For me, it became the best Grand Prix in Formula 1," he said.  Perez's 300th start follows a season away from the grid, a period he said changed his outlook on the intensity and scrutiny of Formula One. "When I stepped away from Formula 1, I realised that not every single moment is that important," Perez said. "What matters is staying balanced, not feeling too high in the good moments and not feeling too low in the bad ones." At Cadillac, Perez said he faces a new kind of challenge as the team looks to establish itself in Formula One. "This is my greatest challenge and my biggest objective: to take Cadillac forward," he said. "We started from the back, and I want to see how far we can go over the coming years." Perez said he wanted to decide for himself when to leave Formula One and to do so while still performing at a high level. "As an athlete, it is very important to me to finish my career on a high note, to leave Formula 1 when I decide to leave, and while still performing at a high level." He added he remained focused on driving rather than a future management role. "When my time as a driver ends, I have always said that I am excited about exploring other areas and learning other things."

Source: Reuters

Oct 27 : Fourth-tier Fleetwood Town beat 10-man Arsenal 5-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in the League Cup last 16 on Tuesday, pulling off a major upset at Highbury Stadium. Aaron Loupalo-Bi put the League Two side ahead in the 21st minute, shrugging off Arsenal defender Marli Salmon before driving a tight-angle effort beyond goalkeeper Illan Meslier. The match had been interrupted early on for more than eight minutes after a drone was spotted above the stadium. Arsenal drew level four minutes after the break through Viktor Gyokeres, who converted from close range after Ceadach O'Neill, making his senior debut, controlled a long ball from Piero Hincapie and delivered into the area.

JERUSALEM: Israel's wartime election appeared deadlocked on Tuesday (Oct 27), exit polls showed, a potential setback for veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu if the projections hold, with neither side having a clear path to power but rival Gadi Eisenkot's larger bloc potentially giving him the first chance to form a government. The stalemate could yet work in Netanyahu's favour, allowing him to remain in power in a caretaker capacity while parties try to forge a governing coalition. Turnout was 77.7 per cent, Israel's Central Elections Committee said, the highest in more than two decades and around 7 percentage points higher than in the previous election in 2022. Israel's three major networks updated their exit polls, giving Eisenkot's bloc a two-seat edge over Netanyahu's Likud-led camp, at 52-50.

The remaining 18 seats were allocated to unaligned Arab parties in the exit polls. But Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, has all but ruled out forming a government with them, complicating his path to a majority despite his bloc's lead. Some Israeli media outlets, including pro-Netanyahu Channel 14, projected a far stronger showing for Netanyahu and his parties, saying they would collectively win 60 seats. Final results could take days, and Israel's fragmented political system leaves smaller parties potential kingmakers. No single party has ever won 61 seats outright in the 120-seat Knesset, making coalitions the norm. It was the first election since the Hamas-led attacks of Oct 7, 2023, and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. Yohanan Plesner, president of the Israel Democracy Institute, called the exit polls a major defeat for Netanyahu's coalition, which they showed falling from 68 seats in the outgoing Knesset to about 50. But he said Eisenkot had not emerged as a clear winner. Plesner cautioned that much could change as votes were counted. If the final result mirrored the exit polls, he said, Eisenkot could try to form a minority government that would remove Netanyahu from power, even if it lasted only until another election. ANTI-NETANYAHU BOOST While there was no clear outcome, the exit polls reflected the strength of the anti-Netanyahu opposition. Opposition leader Yair Lapid said in a statement: “Don’t let anyone confuse you: the Netanyahu bloc has suffered a crushing defeat. This is a total collapse and the public has told them to go home.” Eisenkot, 66, a hawkish former military chief who lost a son and two nephews in the Gaza war, emerged as Netanyahu's strongest challenger, stressing his security credentials while positioning himself as a centrist domestically. He entered politics only four years ago and joined Netanyahu's war cabinet after the 2023 Hamas attack, but quit eight months later, criticising the prime minister's leadership. Eisenkot offers a break with Netanyahu's leadership and far-right allies, but not with the hardline approach to security that has become more entrenched since the 2023 Hamas attack: He opposes Palestinian statehood and says Hamas' military wing must be destroyed or dismantled. Eisenkot says Israel's response - a war that has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians, according to Gaza health authorities - was a failure because Hamas remains in charge. "Dear Democrats, a decision was made," Yair Golan, leader of the Democrats party and a Netanyahu rival, said at a party rally after polls closed. "The nation has given us a sacred duty: to translate the trust they have placed in us into action, to fortify democracy, to save Israel and to provide true defense for the state." The headquarters of the Joint List, an alliance of several Arab parties, burst into whistles and applause when exit polls were released at the close of voting, on a historic night for turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel. “We refuse the occupation and racism, and we will remain here,” said Faten Gattas, a candidate in the Joint List, in a speech at the alliance’s headquarters in Nazareth. Candidates hoped that high Arab voter participation would allow them to play a decisive role in preventing Netanyahu’s coalition - the most far-right in Israel's history - from returning to power.

Related:

Palestinians protest against military demolitions in West Bank as Israelis vote

Netanyahu touts Trump endorsement on eve of vote, suggests they may restart war on Iran

Long lines had formed outside polling stations as voters turned out in huge numbers, grappling with the trauma of Israel's deadliest day, when Hamas killed 1,200 people and took 251 hostage, and the wars in Gaza and with Lebanon's Hezbollah and Iran that followed. While Netanyahu was criticised for the country's biggest security failure, he argued that he had made Israel and the world safer by assassinating top leaders of Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran. The policies of Netanyahu's right-wing coalition have been divisive at home and deepened Israel's international isolation, but he has portrayed himself as the leader with the mettle to face down Israel's foes. Netanyahu, 77, has served as prime minister for nearly 19 of the past 30 years and has repeatedly survived political crises. His opponents have managed to wrest the premiership from him only once since 2009, after four inconclusive elections in two years. Eighteen months later, he was back. He entered the election facing longstanding corruption charges, which he denies, and criticism over intelligence failures that allowed Hamas-led militants to carry out their attack. Netanyahu campaigned on an endorsement from US President Donald Trump, his ally in the war against Iran.

Source: Reuters/fs/dy

Oct 27 : Robinhood Markets missed Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit on Tuesday, as slower cryptocurrency trading and higher expenses overshadowed strong activity in options and prediction markets. Shares of the Menlo Park, California-based company fell 7 per cent in after-hours trading. The trading platform's transaction-based revenue from cryptocurrencies fell 55 per cent to $120 million from a year earlier. Crypto markets have come under pressure this year amid heightened volatility and persistent outflows, as inflationary pressures and higher interest rates make bonds and other traditional investments more attractive than speculative assets.

Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency, has fallen as much as 8 per cent year to date as geopolitical tensions and rising oil prices add to market uncertainty. OPTIONS, EVENT CONTRACTS OFFSET CRYPTO SLUMP Robinhood's overall transaction-based revenue rose about 19 per cent to $867 million, driven by a more than sixfold increase in event-contracts revenue and a 31 per cent jump in options revenue. However, revenue growth lagged the increase in trading contracts, suggesting that growth was becoming more concentrated in a few key areas, said Bill Birmingham, research head at REX Financial. "Prediction markets are becoming a second outlet for the same core active traders rather than a funnel for new customers," Birmingham said, adding that some of the volume may reflect a shift from existing trading activity rather than incremental business. Robinhood CFO Shiv Verma, however, emphasized that prediction markets was an important growth driver for the company. "Prediction markets is almost a $500-million-a-year business already, and so growing incredibly nicely, and it's less than two years old because it came out at the start of the 2024 election," Verma told journalists over a call. He said both sports and non-sports event contracts were growing strongly, with non-sports contracts accounting for a larger share of overall trading volume. The company's operating expenses rose 16 per cent to $739 million for the three months ended September 30, driven by higher credit-loss provisions, spending on new businesses such as Trump Accounts and Rothera, and increased marketing. Robinhood posted a profit of 51 cents per share, missing analysts' expectations of a per-share profit of 55 cents, according to estimates compiled by LSEG.

Oct 27 : Visa beat expectations for fourth-quarter results on Tuesday as customers continued swiping their cards to pay for travel, shopping and dining out despite macroeconomic uncertainty. The results from the world's largest payments processor underscore a robust US economy in the face of persistent inflationary pressures as consumers continue spending, underpinned by a strong labor market and wage growth. "Growth across consumer spend bands remained relatively consistent with prior quarters, with the highest spend band continuing to grow the fastest. We did not see signs of the lower spend consumer weakening in our volumes," Visa finance chief Chris Suh said in a post-earnings call. Payments volume, a gauge of consumer and business spending on Visa's network, jumped 9 per cent in the reported quarter on a constant-dollar basis, while processed transactions rose 10 per cent.

Visa's extensive digital payments network, which spans more than 200 countries and territories, positions it to better endure economic downturns as billions of people globally rely on the card network for everyday spending and other purchases. CLIENT INCENTIVES, PROFIT FORECAST IN FOCUS Client incentives jumped 21 per cent to $5.1 billion in the quarter from the prior year, largely driven by new deals that were signed during the July to September period and early in the fourth quarter. "The one thing to nitpick is client incentives, which were above expectations," Seaport analyst Jeff Cantwell said, adding the development likely impacted Visa's fiscal 2027 forecasts. Suh told analysts incentives growth would step up in fiscal 2027 as Visa is expecting around 25 per cent of its payments volumes to be renewed, including with several large clients. That compares with 20 per cent in fiscal 2026. The company anticipates fiscal 2027 profit per share growth between a low-double-digit and low-teens percentage, while net revenue growth is expected to be in the low-double-digit percentage. "While some may be underwhelmed by the EPS guide, we think it likely reflects... (the management's) decision to keep investing in long-term strategic initiatives to extend the durability of top-line growth," KBW analysts led by Sanjay Sakhrani said. Visa's shares fell about 1.4 per cent in extended trading. The stock has gained 14.6 per cent this year through the last close. On an adjusted basis, it earned $3.48 per share in the three months ended September 30, beating an expectation of $3.44 per share, according to estimates compiled by LSEG. CROSS-BORDER STRENGTH Cross-border volumes excluding intra-Europe, a measure of international travel demand, were a bright spot as they jumped 14 per cent in the quarter on a constant-dollar basis. "It is reflective of strong consumer sentiment, strong demand for travel experiences, and the fact that e-commerce has also just expanded," Suh said. Suh told Reuters travel in and out of the Middle East was also coming back closer to normal levels after being suppressed due to the Iran conflict. The FIFA World Cup, which ran from June 11 to July 19, has also helped boost activity across Visa's network as it brought many visitors to the United States. "XB (cross-border) showed a nice step-up in growth sequentially, and that was one area we were watching for signs of potential weakness going into earnings," Seaport's Cantwell said. Net revenue jumped 13 per cent to $12.1 billion in the quarter. For fiscal year 2026, Visa hauled record net revenue of $46 billion. Rival Mastercard is set to report quarterly earnings later this week.

Source: Reuters

ZURICH, Oct 27 : Logitech International on Tuesday reported a better-than-expected profit for the second quarter, with the computer mouse and keyboard maker seeing higher demand for its gaming and video conferencing devices. The Swiss-U.S. company reported non-GAAP operating income of $231 million for the three months to the end of September, beating forecasts for $204 million in a consensus gathered by Visible Alpha and the company's own guidance for $185 million to $210 million. Sales rose 3 per cent to $1.22 billion, in line with analyst forecasts and towards the upper end of the company's own outlook of $1.19 billion to $1.22 billion. CEO Hanneke Faber said Logitech had come through a difficult period marked by tight component sourcing, higher costs and the conflict in the Middle East.

"Even as global PC shipments declined by 20 per cent in the quarter, our pointing devices and keyboards grew by mid single digits, demonstrating our growth opportunity comes from the large installed PC base," she told analysts on a call. Innovation, including products like matcha and latte-coloured mice, had helped the company grow sales in that category, while 15 new products in the gaming category boosted sales there. Sales of video collaboration equipment rose 12 per cent as business customers refreshed their workplaces after encouraging staff back to the office. "Video collaboration demand is strong and we expect it to continue to be strong," Faber said. "It's not discretionary. You need to refresh those rooms, you need expanded office space if you are going to ask people to come back to work." Faber said there was strong demand from healthcare and government customers. Logitech also said it had suffered a lower-than-expected impact from the forced closure at a factory of one of its semiconductor suppliers at the end of June, which it originally expected to cost it up to $200 million in lost sales in the next quarter. After getting chips from other suppliers, the company said it now expects the impact to be $70 million to $80 million. Logitech said its sales would be in the range of $1.36 billion to $1.43 billion for the three months to the end of December. It also expects non-GAAP operating income of $220 million to $255 million down from $312 million a year earlier, due to higher component and transport costs, as well as the lost sales caused by the factory shutdown.

Source: Reuters
